title: Devil's Throat Rising
premise: Ada Brightwater, a storm chaser deep in debt to the Vane brothers—cheerful lenders who break legs with a smile—accepts a job from her old rival Cass Merrow: guide a survey team into Devil's Throat, a canyon her crew swore off a decade ago after a death they never explained. But the surveyors aren't mapping water; they're hunting a pre-dam cave system that holds proof the state's beloved flood-control project was built on falsified reports, and Cass intends to sell that proof to whoever pays most. When the dry season's first storm floods the canyon early, Ada must choose between destroying the evidence to save her crew, selling it to clear her debts, or giving it to a journalist whose story could ruin the very people she owes. She chooses justice over survival, leaks the findings, and walks out of the Throat broke, hunted, and finally free of measuring life in miles.
about_author: Ivo Underhill is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons running commercial trips through the canyons of the American Southwest before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people whose loyalty is tested by geography, weather, and money.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector Smiles
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The Vane brothers give Ada thirty days to repay a debt she can't cover, just as rival Cass Merrow arrives offering triple rate for a survey run into Devil's Throat—the canyon her old partner died in ten years ago. Needing the money, Ada signs on against her own rule, hiding the truth about the canyon from her crew. Emotional beat: dread dressed up as opportunity.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, Ada's navigator and quiet love. Descending into the Throat, the crew discovers the surveyors are photographing sealed engineering records in a flooded cave—evidence the dam below was built on falsified safety reports. Cass reveals she plans to auction the documents to the construction firm itself. A tremor collapses the exit route behind them. Emotional beat: betrayal hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Dry Season, Rising Water
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Trapped as an early storm sends floodwater surging through the canyon, the crew splits: Cass and the surveyors race for the high route with the evidence, while Ada realizes the Vanes were paid by the firm to bury the job—and them—with it. In the climax, Ada confronts Cass at the cave mouth as the water rises, takes the records, and nearly drowns saving her rival anyway. Emotional beat: love against duty, both nearly lost.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Out of the canyon with nothing but photographs and a deadline, Ada gives everything to journalist Ruth Okonkwo instead of paying the Vanes, gambling that exposure will make her debts worthless and her enemies cautious. The story breaks; the firm folds; the Vanes retreat. Ada and Jonah drive away from the Throat together, broke but unowned. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, and the first year measured in years.
